title: Efficient recovery of aluminum from saline slag wastes
author: Yoldi, Maria
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Activate waste by milling
steps.instruction: Mill the aluminum slag waste to increase its surface area before chemical extraction.

steps.title: Prepare NaOH extraction solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve NaOH in deionized water to obtain an aqueous solution of either 1 mol dm⁻³ or 2 mol dm⁻³, according to the experimental plan.

steps.title: First NaOH extraction under reflux
steps.instruction: Combine the milled waste with the prepared NaOH solution, place the mixture on a reflux apparatus, and stir for the selected extraction time (1 h, 2 h, or 4 h).

steps.title: Repeat extraction for consecutive steps
steps.instruction: Perform up to three additional extraction cycles (total of four consecutive steps), each time adding fresh NaOH solution of the chosen concentration, refluxing and stirring for the same set of times (1 h, 2 h, or 4 h) to further solubilize Al³⁺.

steps.title: Filter to separate aqueous phase
steps.instruction: After each extraction cycle, filter the reaction mixture to collect the aqueous solution containing extracted Al³⁺ and retain the solid residual waste.

steps.title: Record aluminum extraction yields
steps.instruction: Measure the aluminum concentration in each filtrate; the first extraction can yield up to 7.54 g dm⁻³ Al, and the cumulative amount after four steps may reach 9.59 g dm⁻³.

steps.title: Characterize residual waste
steps.instruction: Analyze the filtered solid waste by N₂ adsorption at –196 °C, X‑ray diffraction, X‑ray fluorescence, energy‑dispersive X‑ray spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy.
